subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Reactivity 2.2 HL: Rate laws and mechanisms
Reactivity 2.3 HL: The equilibrium constant Kc

questions.q: A rate law of the form rate = k[A]^m[B]^n shows that the orders m and n:
questions.explain: Reaction orders are found from experimental rate data, not from the balanced equation.

questions.q: If doubling [A] doubles the rate, the order with respect to A is:
questions.explain: Rate proportional to [A]^1 means doubling [A] doubles the rate.

questions.q: If doubling [B] quadruples the rate, the order with respect to B is:
questions.explain: Rate proportional to [B]^2 means doubling [B] increases rate by 2^2 = 4.

questions.q: If changing [C] has no effect on the rate, the order with respect to C is:
questions.explain: A zero-order reactant does not appear in the rate law.

questions.q: The overall order of a reaction is:
options: The sum of the individual orders
questions.explain: Overall order = m + n + ... from the rate law.

questions.q: The rate-determining step of a reaction mechanism is:
questions.explain: The slowest step limits the overall rate, so the rate law reflects the species involved up to and including it.

questions.q: The units of the rate constant k for a first-order reaction are:
questions.explain: For a first-order reaction rate = k[A], so k has units of s^-1.

questions.q: The Arrhenius equation shows that the rate constant k increases when:
options: Temperature increases or activation energy decreases
questions.explain: k rises with higher temperature and lower activation energy, explaining faster rates.

questions.q: For the equilibrium H2(g) + I2(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), the expression for Kc is:
questions.explain: Products over reactants, each raised to its coefficient; HI has a coefficient of 2.

questions.q: A very small value of Kc (much less than 1) indicates that at equilibrium:
questions.explain: A small Kc means the equilibrium position lies towards the reactants.

questions.q: The value of Kc for a given reaction changes only with:
questions.explain: Kc is constant at a fixed temperature; only temperature changes its value.

questions.q: If Kc = 1 for a reaction, at equilibrium the reaction quotient shows that:
options: Products and reactants terms are balanced (comparable amounts)
questions.explain: Kc = 1 indicates neither side is strongly favoured.

questions.q: For a reaction rate = k[A][B], the overall order is:
questions.explain: Orders 1 + 1 = 2 overall.

questions.q: Intermediates that are formed and used up during a mechanism:
options: Do not appear in the overall balanced equation
questions.explain: Intermediates cancel out because they are produced in one step and consumed in another.

questions.q: Adding a catalyst to a reaction at equilibrium changes Kc by:
questions.explain: A catalyst speeds attainment of equilibrium but does not alter Kc or the equilibrium position.

questions.q: For a zero-order reactant, a graph of concentration against time is:
options: A straight line with negative gradient
questions.explain: Zero-order reactants are consumed at a constant rate, giving a linear decrease.

questions.q: When temperature increases for an exothermic reaction, Kc:
questions.explain: For an exothermic reaction, higher temperature shifts equilibrium back, lowering Kc.

questions.q: The molecularity of an elementary step is the:
options: Number of species that collide in that step
questions.explain: Molecularity (unimolecular, bimolecular) describes species in a single elementary step.

questions.q: If the reaction quotient Q is less than Kc, the reaction will:
options: Proceed forward to form more products
questions.explain: When Q < Kc, the system shifts forward until Q equals Kc.

questions.q: A reaction is found to be first order in A and zero order in B. Its rate law is:
questions.explain: Zero order in B means B does not appear; first order in A gives rate = k[A].
